name: Motorized Bicycle
description: A pedal bicycle with an electric motor that assists while pedaling or runs on a throttle, up to 28 mph on a flat surface, or with a helper motor under 50 cc or rated at no more than 1.5 brake horsepower; the Motor Vehicle Commission calls it a moped.

restrictions.rule: A pedal bicycle: an electric motor that assists while the rider pedals or propels it on a throttle, with a top motor-powered speed of 28 mph on a flat surface; or a helper motor under 50 cc or rated at no more than 1.5 brake horsepower (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1)
A throttle e-bike, or a pedal-assist e-bike that keeps assisting past 20 mph, lands here rather than in the low-speed electric bicycle category (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, as amended by P.L.2025, c.285)
One with pedals, a motor capable of more than 750 watts and a top speed over 28 mph is an electric motorized bicycle, which the law counts as a motorcycle (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1)
Riders must be 15 or older; riders 15 and 16 need a moped (class F) license, and riders 17 and older need any driver's license or a moped license (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3)
The moped license takes a knowledge test and a riding demonstration (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3)
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission, with two plate stickers on the front fork (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3i)
One not registrable before P.L.2025, c.285 had a grace period to register
The owner must carry liability insurance, and the rider must carry the license, registration and insurance card (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3, 39:4-14.3e)
Barred from interstate highways, highways divided by a median, highways posted over 50 mph, and public land where the agency in charge prohibits it (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3)
Bicycle rules otherwise apply, and on a road the rider has the duties of a vehicle driver (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3)
Selling a kit that turns a low-speed electric bicycle into a motorized bicycle is prohibited (P.L.2025, c.285)
